top_rules: JAVA-SEC-08 stays SHOULD: find-sec-bugs is maintained (commits into 2026-03), not abandoned — verify via grep for `findsecbugs` alongside a bound SpotBugs execution.

Add a version-pin clause: never let `com.github.spotbugs` Gradle plugin resolve to 6.4.1/6.4.2 (SpotBugs 4.9.5/4.9.6) with find-sec-bugs on the classpath — confirmed `NoSuchMethodError` crash, fixed only on 6.4.3+/SpotBugs 4.9.7+.

All eight XXE_* rules stay MUST but add a reading heuristic: hardening call must be in the same method as the factory construction — find-sec-bugs and SonarJava both miss cross-method hardening (maintainer-confirmed, issue #738).
COMMAND_INJECTION stays MUST with a grep-only fallback that fully substitutes for the tool: Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder with concatenated or formatted single-string args.

PATH_TRAVERSAL_IN/OUT stay MUST; carry the tool's own 'potential finding' caveat into the rule — verify attacker control of the path before treating a hit as real, and grep archive-extraction loops directly since under-reporting is possible.
PREDICTABLE_RANDOM stays MUST but demote tool dependency to optional — neither Semgrep p/java nor the verified SonarJava subset has an equivalent rule; the grep is a complete standalone check.

Require CI to fail loudly (not ignoreFailures) on spotbugsMain/spotbugsTest — find-sec-bugs is provided-scope, so a transitive SpotBugs core bump can reintroduce the crash with no local diff to review.
Do not cite SonarJava as covering PREDICTABLE_RANDOM/COMMAND_INJECTION/PATH_TRAVERSAL until each rule key is individually fetched — only S2755 (XXE) was verified live in this pass.
surprises: find-sec-bugs 1.14.0 has a confirmed, reproduced NoSuchMethodError crash (not just a false-positive/staleness issue) against SpotBugs 4.9.5/4.9.6, caused by SpotBugs itself deleting a method it depended on — SpotBugs reverted the deletion within weeks, citing find-sec-bugs by name in its own PR.

The deprecated method SpotBugs restored is scheduled for permanent removal ~1 year after 2025-10-08 (i.e. around October 2026, about a month after this research date), and find-sec-bugs's own unreleased master has already removed its usage — but no release has shipped that fix, so the public artifact will likely break again on schedule.

Semgrep's public java ruleset explicitly cites find-sec-bugs.github.io/bugs.htm as the source-rule-url for ~24 of its 60 rules — Semgrep is not an independent alternative but a partial port of find-sec-bugs's own taxonomy, and it has zero rules for SchemaFactory/Validator/XMLReader/XPath XXE or PREDICTABLE_RANDOM.

find-sec-bugs ships its SpotBugs dependency as provided scope, meaning the consumer's own toolVersion pin — not find-sec-bugs's declared version — determines actual runtime compatibility; the tool's own pom.xml version number is nearly irrelevant to whether it will crash.

The exact same XXE cross-method false-negative (hardening applied in a helper method is invisible to the detector) was independently confirmed in both find-sec-bugs (#738) and SonarJava (S2755 community thread) — it's a structural limitation of single-method dataflow analysis shared across tools, not a find-sec-bugs-specific defect.

top_rules: Verdict: ship kotlin-quality/errors-and-resources.md as a 28th depth file, family KT-ERR, rows KT-ERR-01..05 — five rows clears the 'not two or three' bar
KT-ERR-01: never wrap Error-propagating or test-assertion code in runCatching{} — it catches Throwable not Exception, and is inline so no catch-clause lint ever sees inside it

KT-ERR-02: re-interrupt/rethrow a caught InterruptedException even via runCatching — detekt's SwallowedException whitelists InterruptedException by default, so no promotion closes this gap; reading-heuristic only
KT-ERR-03: use{} never reaches Sequence or Flow (neither implements AutoCloseable) — keep and close the underlying Stream/handle explicitly
KT-ERR-03: a suspending close() called from finally/onCompletion after cancellation must be wrapped in withContext(NonCancellable){} or it never runs
KT-ERR-04: keep detekt's SwallowedException/ThrowingNewInstanceOfSameException active — they already catch throw X(e.message) instead of throw X(e), active by default unlike Java's UnusedException
KT-ERR-05: promote detekt's ExitOutsideMain (ships active:false) to catch System.exit/Runtime.exit/Runtime.halt/exitProcess outside main in one rule
@Throws placement is M-V-04/KT-INTEROP's row and Result-as-public-return-type is M-V-07/KT-API's row — cite both, add no new KT-ERR rows for them
surprises: detekt's SwallowedException default config whitelists InterruptedException as 'nonexceptional' — the opposite gap direction from Java, where JAVA-ERR-01's mistake at least has an off-by-default Error Prone check to promote; no detekt rule ID exists for this at all

detekt's default gate is stronger than Java's for exception-chaining: SwallowedException (catches throw X(e.message)) is active by default, while Java's equivalent UnusedException is in Error Prone's DISABLED_CHECKS and must be promoted

runCatching's inlining means it never appears as a KtCatchClause at the call site, so every catch-clause-keyed detekt rule (SwallowedException, TooGenericExceptionCaught, EmptyCatchBlock) is structurally blind to it regardless of activation state

SuspendFunSwallowedCancellation (KT-CORO-01's sibling measurement) only fires when a suspend call happens inside runCatching's lambda — a non-suspend runCatching swallowing an Error/AssertionError has zero coverage under any detekt config

kotlin.Result's -Xallow-result-return-type restriction is fully historical (removed in Kotlin 1.5, 2021) yet still shows up in search results as if live — worth flagging explicitly so drafters don't cite it as current
ktlint's 404'd public rules-doc page required falling back to reading the actual rule-class directory in the pinned exemplar clone, which is a stronger source anyway

JAVA-SEC-02 — Resolve jackson-databind to ≥2.18.8/2.21.4/3.1.4 AND configure an allow-list PTV wherever polymorphic typing exists; check the resolved version, never the config. (MUST, unchanged)
JAVA-SEC-03 — Harden every XML parser factory independently and IN THE SAME METHOD that constructs it; a clean tool run is not evidence of safety. (MUST, CHANGED — overclaim fix)
JAVA-SEC-04 — Never pass an attacker-influenced string to Context.lookup() or any javax.naming/JDO/JMX/rowset lookup API. (MUST, unchanged)
JAVA-SEC-05 — Resolve-and-verify containment before opening any stream over a caller-supplied path segment; treat find-sec-bugs hits as "potential" and its silence as no clearance. (MUST, CHANGED)
JAVA-SEC-06 — Build every subprocess command with the array/varargs ProcessBuilder form; never Runtime.exec(String), never "sh","-c",cmd+arg. (MUST, CHANGED — grep stated as the severity floor)

JAVA-SEC-08 — Add find-sec-bugs wherever SpotBugs gates a module handling untrusted input, scoped to those modules, treating the tool as maintained-but-fragile. (SHOULD, CHANGED — floor corrected to plugin 6.4.3+)

JAVA-SEC-10 — Where find-sec-bugs is wired, pin the SpotBugs core it runs against (never plugin 6.4.1/6.4.2) and never let ignoreFailures/failOnError swallow the gate. (MUST where wired, NEW)
JAVA-ERR-01 — Re-interrupt or propagate every caught InterruptedException, including one caught implicitly by a wider catch. (MUST, CHANGED — names KT-ERR-02)

JAVA-ERR-03 — Acquire every Closeable/AutoCloseable inside try-with-resources, including Files.walk/list/lines/find streams and wrapping streams. (MUST, CHANGED — names KT-ERR-03)

KT-ERR-01 — Never wrap code that must propagate a JVM Error or a test assertion in runCatching { }; it catches Throwable and no detekt rule can see inside it. (MUST, NEW)
KT-ERR-02 — Re-interrupt or rethrow every caught InterruptedException in Kotlin, and state in the rule that no detekt rule ID exists for it. (MUST, NEW)
KT-ERR-03 — Call .use { } on every AutoCloseable; close the handle explicitly behind any Sequence or Flow, and wrap a suspending close() in withContext(NonCancellable). (MUST, NEW)
KT-ERR-04 — Never write SomeException(e.message) where SomeException(e) is meant; keep detekt's SwallowedException and ThrowingNewInstanceOfSameException active. (MUST, NEW)

top_rules: Pair every annotationProcessorPaths declaration with <maven.compiler.proc>full</maven.compiler.proc> (compiler-plugin >=3.13.0) or JDK 23+ silently runs zero processors

Verification for that rule must assert target/generated-sources/annotations/ is non-empty, not just grep the POM -- a green mvn verify cannot distinguish processors-ran from processors-silently-skipped
Never say 'JDK 21' disables implicit annotation processing -- JDK 21/22 only warn; JDK 23 (JDK-8321319) is the release that actually flips the default to -proc:none
<proc>full</proc> is only a legal value from maven-compiler-plugin 3.13.0 (MCOMPILER-548) even though the proc parameter itself dates to 2.2

Gradle needs no matching GRADLE-TOOL row: gradle/gradle's JavaCompilerArgumentsBuilder.java unconditionally emits -proc:none or -processorpath on every JavaCompile, immune since the 5.0 annotationProcessor/classpath split

Apache's own maven-toolchains-plugin only selects from toolchains.xml and never downloads a JDK (confirmed from ToolchainMojo.java source: no skip param, no fetch code) -- auto-provisioning needs a different, third-party plugin

Name org.mvnsearch:toolchains-maven-plugin (Foojay-backed download) explicitly and never transpose it with org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-toolchains-plugin (select-only) -- the names are word-order swaps of each other
-Dtoolchain.skip belongs only to org.mvnsearch:toolchains-maven-plugin; Apache's official plugin has no skip parameter at all, so the flag is a silent no-op unless that specific plugin is bound
surprises: The JDK-23 policy change was deferred mid-flight: proposed for JDK 22 (JDK-8306819), reverted to warning-only for that release (JDK-8321321), then reinstated a full release later for JDK 23 (JDK-8321319) -- three bug IDs for what reads as one release-note line
The origin motive is a supply-chain security concern (an unwitting dependency-shipped annotation processor auto-executing at compile time), not a build-hygiene cleanup

apache/maven's own POM shows both sides of the fix in one repo: pom.xml:135 sets proc=full reactor-wide, and submodule api/maven-api-di/pom.xml:34 explicitly overrides back to proc=none because that module only defines annotations and never processes them

Maven's toolchain story needs two rules, not one, because guava genuinely runs javac/javadoc on JDK 26 while Surefire tests the same build on JDK 8/11/17/25 via jdkToolchain -- a real, not hypothetical, split-JDK build

guava's own CI comment reveals the mechanism itself: -Dtoolchain.skip only works because actions/setup-java pre-installs every JDK the org.mvnsearch plugin would otherwise fetch -- a bare local mvn verify still needs that plugin (or a hand-built toolchains.xml)

org.mvnsearch:toolchains-maven-plugin's Central metadata last-updated timestamp (April 2023) is years older than every other plugin queried here despite guava pinning its newest version, flagging an ecosystem-maturity risk for a mechanism the rule set would otherwise recommend as the standard fix

MVN-BUILD-02 — Declare every annotation processor in `<annotationProcessorPaths>` with an explicit version, and pair it with MVN-BUILD-16 (REVISED: rationale now version-stamped JDK ≤22 vs 23+; verification gained the artifact check).

MVN-BUILD-16 — NEW: set `<maven.compiler.proc>full</maven.compiler.proc>` (plugin ≥ 3.13.0, else `-proc:full` in `<compilerArgs>`) in every module declaring a processor, and verify by asserting `target/generated-sources/annotations/` is non-empty, never by the POM alone.
MVN-BUILD-17 — NEW: name JDK 23 as the release where implicit annotation processing stops; never "JDK 21", never "modern JDKs"; `<proc>none</proc>` is the explicit opt-out.

MVN-BUILD-19 — NEW: keep `org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-toolchains-plugin` (select-only) and `org.mvnsearch:toolchains-maven-plugin` (Foojay downloader) apart; never claim Apache's plugin provisions a JDK and never write `-Dtoolchain.skip` unless the mvnsearch plugin is bound.
MVN-BUILD-20 — NEW: set `<jdkToolchain>` inside `maven-surefire-plugin`'s own configuration to test on another JDK; never widen the reactor toolchain and never hardcode `<jvm>`.
MVN-ANT-01 — Set `includeantruntime="false"` explicitly on every live `<javac>` before any other change to the file.
MVN-ANT-02 — Never introduce `ant.importBuild()`; bridge via an external process or `ant.<task>()` inside a real task action.
MVN-ANT-03 — Never "change" an Ant property by re-declaring it; properties are write-once.
MVN-ANT-04 — Do not read a `depends` chain as proof a target ran.
MVN-ANT-05 — Port leaf targets first and verify each ported artifact against the Ant build's own jar before deleting the Ant target.
MVN-ANT-06 — Pin `digestalg`/`sigalg` on `<signjar>` and set `preservelastmodified="true"`.

top_rules: withPluginClasspath() DOES reach settings scope — the injected-classpath resolver is wired at Scope.Build and consulted by DefaultPluginRequestApplicator regardless of PluginManagerInternal target type (source-confirmed; zero exemplars actually use it)

The compileOnly x withPluginClasspath trap (GRADLE-PLUG-14) is the identical defect object at settings scope, not an analogue — one shared ClassPath, one shared resolver, same ClassNotFoundException naming the wrong class

No API or build-scan value reports BuildService instantiation count; 'created exactly once' can only be proven via a marker file the service writes on first use, read back after build() — never a static counter
GradleRunner.withDebug(true) breaks TestKit's process isolation and would make an in-process static readable, but is a rejected pattern — a debug aid, not a sanctioned assertion path

GRADLE-PLUG-10's existing --configuration-cache functional-test leg structurally already covers GRADLE-PLUG-23's 'Reusing configuration cache.' verification for a Settings plugin, since the settings file is the only place it can ever be applied

GRADLE-PLUG-24 (sha256 enforcement) needs a runnable negative test — tamper the pin, assert buildAndFail() — because a grep for MessageDigest proves the check exists, not that anything ever calls .get() on it

Isolated Projects diagnostics mode routes through the same store-then-discard configuration-cache reporting pipeline, making BuildResult.output a legal TestKit assertion surface for GRADLE-PLUG-27, though the exact console phrase is an unpinned dated re-check
GRADLE-PLUG-22 and GRADLE-PLUG-26 keep pure reading heuristics, explicitly labeled as such — no dynamic TestKit assertion adds independent signal over a source grep for those two
surprises: No corpus exemplar (ktor's build-settings-logic, junit-framework's settings-conventions) and no gradle/gradle-own TestKit integration test ever applies a plugin from a functional test's generated settings.gradle — the mechanism is real but completely unexercised anywhere in the ecosystem read

Gradle's own ConfigurationCacheTestKitIntegrationTest.groovy carries a doc comment explicitly naming both plugin-resolution routes (INJECTED_CLASSPATH via DefaultInjectedClasspathPluginResolver, MAVEN_REPO via DefaultScriptClassPathResolver) and parametrizes every test case over both — direct source confirmation of Q1/Q4 nobody had to infer

There is no Gradle API, javadoc, or build-scan surface anywhere that reports how many times a shared BuildService was instantiated — registerIfAbsent's 'exactly once' is a construction-time guarantee, not an introspectable fact, so the assertion pattern (a marker file) had to be constructed rather than found

GradleRunner.withDebug(true) genuinely breaks TestKit's process-isolation guarantee (same-JVM execution for IDE debugging) and would make an in-process static field readable — a real, previously undocumented loophole worth explicitly rejecting rather than ignoring

Isolated Projects diagnostics mode doesn't have its own reporting channel — gradle/gradle's own IsolatedProjectsFixture shows it forwards to assertStateStoredAndDiscarded, i.e. it reuses the configuration-cache problem pipeline, which is what makes it TestKit-assertable at all via BuildResult.output

sha256 enforcement (GRADLE-PLUG-24) has a laziness failure mode a static grep can never catch: a Provider computed inside a ValueSource that nothing ever calls .get() on passes every grep while enforcing nothing at runtime, which only a tamper-and-assert-buildAndFail() negative test exposes

Resolved with a marker-file leg, and `withDebug(true)`/static counters explicitly rejected (they defeat the process isolation GRADLE-PLUG-15 requires).

Dated re-check, not a research round — Isolated Projects' diagnostics console wording is unpinned by any primary source (IP incubating since 9.7.0, 2026-08-06); re-confirm and freeze a literal string in GRADLE-PLUG-27 when IP leaves incubating.

top_rules: Size pools by workload regime: CPU-bound stays on a pool sized to availableProcessors() (or the common pool); blocking-style I/O goes one-virtual-thread-per-task — JEP 444 states the CPU-bound exclusion verbatim, not an inference (new JAVA-CONC-15)

Annotate shared mutable state with @GuardedBy from com.google.errorprone.annotations.concurrent or javax.annotation.concurrent — never net.jcip.annotations.GuardedBy, which compiles but the checker silently ignores (new JAVA-CONC-16)

@Immutable (ImmutableChecker) and @GuardedBy (GuardedByChecker) are both ENABLED_ERRORS already — zero config, on by default; @ThreadSafe has no working checker in the public distribution despite its own javadoc's claim

Bound ReentrantReadWriteLock reader fan-out under virtual threads below 65,535 (its own javadoc's documented ceiling, not a newsletter claim) or use StampedLock directly — asReadWriteLock() drops Condition support, reentrancy, and ownership (new JAVA-CONC-17)

Bump DoubleCheckedLocking, DateFormatConstant, and FutureReturnValueIgnored to -Xep:Name:ERROR — all three are ENABLED_WARNINGS already, so this is a severity bump, not an activation (extends JAVA-LINT-02)
DC_DOUBLECHECK runs automatically the moment JAVA-LINT-10 wires SpotBugs at all — findbugs.xml's FindDoubleCheck detector carries no disabled="true" (extends JAVA-LINT-10, no new config needed)
Drop M-N-06 as a standalone rule: close() semantics is JAVA-ERR-05, VT admission control is JAVA-CONC-01/02, pool-sizing regime is the new JAVA-CONC-15 — nothing left to write

A CompletableFuture chain returned to a caller (not discarded as a bare statement) is correct without a terminal handler — FutureReturnValueIgnored targets the fire-and-forget-statement shape specifically, confirmed against a real exemplar
surprises: @ThreadSafe's own javadoc claims ThreadSafeChecker validation, but ThreadSafeChecker is never imported into BuiltInCheckerSuppliers.java (0 matches vs. 8 wired sibling threadsafety.* checkers) — the annotation's documented enforcement does not actually ship

GuardedByChecker recognizes exactly five annotation packages, and net.jcip.annotations.GuardedBy — the package from Java Concurrency in Practice, the textbook most training data quotes — is not one of them
GuardedByChecker and ImmutableChecker are both ENABLED_ERRORS (fully on, zero config) already; the real gap for M-N-10 is that nothing makes an agent write the annotation, not enforcement

The ReentrantReadWriteLock 65,535 ceiling has a primary source right in its own JDK javadoc's 'Implementation Notes' — the newsletter the topic map flagged as thin didn't need to be the citation at all

FutureReturnValueIgnored's real target is a discarded fire-and-forget statement, not every CompletableFuture chain lacking a terminal handler — a chain returned to a caller transfers responsibility and is correct, confirmed in micronaut-core's AsyncInterceptor
M-N-06 fully dissolves into three existing/new rules (JAVA-ERR-05, JAVA-CONC-01/02, new JAVA-CONC-15) with nothing left over for its own row

conflicts_resolved: JAVA-CONC-13 overclaimed: 'Do not use ForkJoinPool.commonPool() for a blocking callback' was unconditional, but the JDK ships ForkJoinPool.ManagedBlocker as a sanctioned escape hatch that expands pool parallelism for the blocking call's duration. Rule text amended in place to name it as the one exception; rationale now also records that CompletableFuture's no-Executor ...Async default IS that same common pool.

Wrong number corrected: this file's old open question 1 called it the 'ReentrantReadWriteLock 65,536-reader ceiling'. The lock's own javadoc ('Implementation Notes', JDK 21, unchanged since JDK 5) says 65535 recursive write locks and 65535 read locks, and the failure is an Error throw. Corrected everywhere; the wrong figure's only home (open question 1) was removed.

Residual dive vs. virtual-threads dive on structured-concurrency status: the residual's Contested section says 'still preview as of JDK 25, JEP 505 in JDK 25'. The vt dive read the full seven-preview changelog (JEP 505/25, 525/26, 533/27, finalisation targeted at 28). Primary-source changelog outranks a passing status aside; JAVA-CONC-05/06 unchanged, conflict recorded in verdict 16.

Map row M-N-07's framing ('CompletableFuture chains with no terminal handler') narrowed: a chain RETURNED to a caller or assigned to a field transfers exception-handling responsibility and is correct (micronaut-core AsyncInterceptor:100-102 confirms). Only a bare unassigned statement is the bug. Row therefore lands as a JAVA-LINT severity bump, not a reading-heuristic rule here.

Enable-vs-bump, third instance: DoubleCheckedLocking, DateFormatConstant and FutureReturnValueIgnored are ENABLED_WARNINGS (BuiltInCheckerSuppliers.java:982, 972, 1015), not DISABLED_CHECKS. 'Enable it' asks an agent to do nothing; the action is -Xep:<Name>:ERROR. Same shape as frame correction 30's StringCaseLocaleUsage.

@ThreadSafe's own javadoc contradicted by source: it claims validation by ThreadSafeChecker, which is imported into none of BuiltInCheckerSuppliers.java's three built-in sets (0 matches vs 8 wired threadsafety.* siblings). Resolved against the javadoc; JAVA-CONC-16 states it is prose only, and verdict 12 records it as a documented GAP.
needs_another_round: Kotlin Flow (map rows M-U-07, M-U-10) — does Flow need its own depth section with the catch-operator placement rule and the StateFlow conflation contract, or do two rows in coroutines.md cover it? Unchanged from the previous round; this dive did not touch Kotlin.

JDK 27 GA re-verification — JDK 27 reached GA 2026-09-15, after every JEP 533 claim here was written against the RC. Did the 7th preview's shape (R_X type parameter, timeout(), awaitAll() removed) ship unchanged, and is structured concurrency still targeted at JDK 28?

detekt activation defaults — the audited snapshot is a main-branch build mid-package-rename (dev.detekt.*). Do the four coroutine rules stay active:false in the first stable release from that branch? KT-CORO-01's whole premise depends on it.

Error Prone ThreadSafeChecker registration — re-read BuiltInCheckerSuppliers.java's import list on any Error Prone bump past 2.36.0. If ThreadSafeChecker appears, JAVA-CONC-16's '@ThreadSafe is prose only' clause inverts. New question opened by this round.
rule_ids: JAVA-CONC-01 — Never construct a fixed-size pool of virtual threads; bound concurrency with a Semaphore instead. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-02 — Bound fan-out at the downstream resource's real capacity, never at the task count. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-03 — State synchronized-vs-ReentrantLock conditionally on the module's minimum JDK, never as one sentence. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-04 — Never use -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads; read the jdk.VirtualThreadPinned JFR event instead. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-05 — Keep every preview API off the main sourceset compile path of any published module. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-06 — Stamp every StructuredTaskScope/Joiner member you emit with the JDK it was verified against. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-07 — Carry context with ScopedValue, not ThreadLocal, and never pass a literal null to orElse. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-08 — State a strategy for every static final ThreadLocal cache before scaling onto virtual threads; do not default to a lock-free pool. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-09 — Inject a ProcessLauncher at every spawn point; never call new ProcessBuilder().start() outside the one real implementation. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-10 — Drain getInputStream() and getErrorStream() concurrently; never read one to completion first. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-11 — Run the destroy/waitFor/destroyForcibly ladder from a finally on every spawn path, walking descendants() if the CLI forks. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-12 — clear() ProcessBuilder.environment() before writing to it, and read System.getenv() in exactly one classified place. (unchanged)

JAVA-CONC-13 — Make Process.onExit() the async path and pass an explicit bounded Executor to every blocking stage; the common pool's only exception is a ManagedBlocker. (AMENDED — ManagedBlocker carve-out added, shared-common-pool rationale added)
JAVA-CONC-14 — Retry sysexit 75 inside the spawn call, before any exception object for that attempt is constructed. (unchanged)
JAVA-CONC-15 — Size a pool by its workload's regime: CPU-bound on availableProcessors(), blocking I/O one-virtual-thread-per-task, never the reverse. (NEW)
JAVA-CONC-16 — Annotate guarded state with a checker-recognised @GuardedBy package, never net.jcip.annotations, and treat @ThreadSafe as prose only. (NEW)
JAVA-CONC-17 — Bound readers below ReentrantReadWriteLock's 65535-hold ceiling under virtual-thread fan-out, and audit before swapping in asReadWriteLock(). (NEW)
KT-CORO-01 — Explicitly activate detekt's four coroutine rules in the committed config; 'detekt is applied' is not 'these run'. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-02 — Fix bare GlobalScope.launch/async; the context-carrying adapter form is the one named exception. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-03 — Never call runBlocking from inside a suspend fun. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-04 — Install a CoroutineExceptionHandler only on a root coroutine, never on async and never nested. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-05 — Rethrow CancellationException from every catch wide enough to observe it, runCatching included. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-06 — Give each blocking call site a Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(n) view sized to the resource it guards. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-07 — Fix a shared-mutable-state race with atomics, confinement or Mutex.withLock — never with @Volatile. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-08 — Wrap must-complete suspending cleanup in withContext(NonCancellable). (unchanged)
KT-CORO-09 — Put a suspension point or an explicit isActive/ensureActive() check in every long-running coroutine loop. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-10 — Inject the dispatcher in a library or SDK rather than hardcoding it at the call site. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-11 — Back any thread-safety claim with a real-dispatcher stress test; runTest alone cannot fail on a race. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-12 — Launch anything that must outlive a runTest body on backgroundScope. (unchanged)
KT-CORO-13 — Pick StandardTestDispatcher when the test asserts dispatch order; UnconfinedTestDispatcher only when it does not. (unchanged)

top_rules: Use contrib_rules_jvm's java_junit5_test / java_test_suite(runner="junit5") for JUnit 5 under Bazel — no first-party rules_java equivalent exists
A hand-rolled java_test + custom launcher main_class is viable but must reimplement XML_OUTPUT_FILE, TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY, TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE and TEST_SHARD_* to behave like a real Bazel test
java_test_suite's runner attribute defaults to "junit4", not "junit5" — always pass it explicitly for Jupiter sources

Adopting java_junit5_test/java_test_suite never requires calling lint_setup()/linter.register() — apple_rules_lint is only load-bearing for the checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs wrappers (BZL-JAVA-23's CONSIDER), not the test rules

apple_rules_lint is transitively fetched once contrib_rules_jvm is a bazel_dep (its own MODULE.bazel deps on it unconditionally) but fetching is not using — no lint targets generate without an explicit lint_setup call
bazel coverage --combined_report=lcov //... is the only Java coverage path; output is one merged lcov file at $(bazel info output_path)/_coverage/_coverage_report.dat, never JaCoCo XML/CSV
Bazel has no coverage-threshold flag at all (no --fail_under/--minimum_coverage) and no per-target coverage signal — any numeric floor is necessarily a CI-side script over the combined lcov report
A JaCoCo-BRANCH-percentage-style floor (JAVA-TEST-10) cannot read Bazel's lcov output directly — the artifact shapes don't match, so Gradle-side coverage-gate patterns don't transfer to Bazel
surprises: java_junit5_test is literally java_test underneath (main_class=JUnit5Runner + a -javaagent blocking System.exit) — reading the macro source directly settles the 'hand-rolled second path' question: contrib_rules_jvm's own ActualRunner.java IS that second path, and it's ~150 lines to be Bazel-protocol-correct, not five.

apple_rules_lint is still transitively resolved via bzlmod even though the test rules don't need it — a nuance beyond the README's clean 'linting is opt-in' framing (fetched vs. used are different things).

Bazel's own coverage doc for Java is a single sentence with zero mention of JaCoCo; the actual JaCoCo wiring (JacocoCoverageRunner, JACOCO_METADATA_JAR) exists only in Bazel's source, never in any prose doc.

bazelbuild/bazel#12159 (richer JVM coverage format) was closed not_planned in 2024 — the coverage-format gap this dive documents is a deliberate, acknowledged non-goal for Bazel core, not an oversight.
0/6 Bazel-carrying exemplars, including bazelbuild/bazel building itself, set any coverage flag in .bazelrc — the one repo best positioned to need custom Java coverage wiring has none.

Bazel coverage output is lcov-only ('At this point only LCOV is supported') — a genuine format mismatch with every other JVM coverage tool this program covers (JaCoCo, Kover), with no first-party bridge.

conflicts_resolved: BZL-JAVA-23 overclaimed what the apple_rules_lint dependency means — its old text required 'record the apple_rules_lint dependency explicitly' and its grep flagged a bare `bazel_dep(name = "contrib_rules_jvm")` / `bazel_dep(name = "apple_rules_lint")` as a review finding. That would have made the JUnit 5 adoption BZL-JAVA-24 now requires a finding against itself. Rewritten in place: the decision is the `lint_setup()`/`linter.register()` call only, a transitive fetch is explicitly not evidence of adoption, severity stays CONSIDER.

BZL-JAVA-23's dangling clause 'Its java_test_suite and java_junit5_test are a separate, unblocked decision' removed — that decision is now settled by BZL-JAVA-24 (use them) and BZL-JAVA-25 (they carry no lint coupling).

Open question 7 ('Bazel-Java testing and coverage') answered and removed. Its testing half became rules BZL-JAVA-24/25/27; its coverage half had no mechanism to regulate, so it moved into the Verdict as documented gap item 13 (lcov-only, one combined report, no threshold flag in Bazel at all, bazelbuild/bazel#12159 closed not_planned) rather than being dropped or left open.

JAVA-TEST-10's JaCoCo-BRANCH coverage floor was implicitly assumed portable to Bazel; BZL-JAVA-26 records it is not — the artifact shapes do not match and a CI step globbing jacocoTestReport.xml after `bazel coverage` passes vacuously.

Evidence class made explicit rather than averaged: new 'Unmeasured in the corpus' subsection records that BZL-JAVA-24/25/27 have zero exemplars on either side (0/6 reference contrib_rules_jvm, apple_rules_lint, junit.jupiter or junit5) and that BZL-JAVA-26's evidence is one-sided, so a reader cannot mistake source-reading guidance for measured practice.
needs_another_round: java_export / Maven Central publishing from Bazel — does rules_jvm_external's java_export/maven_publish produce a Central-Portal-acceptable bundle (sources jar, javadoc jar, per-file GPG signature, complete POM), or is Bazel a non-publisher that always hands off to Gradle or Maven? Load-bearing for the OCX SDK's jvm-release skill. (carried, unchanged)

KotlinCompile worker-state reproducibility — does building twice with and without --strategy=KotlinCompile=local produce byte-identical jars? Would promote BZL-JAVA-20 from CONSIDER to SHOULD or retire it. Below the line for this program. (carried, unchanged)

contrib_rules_jvm stability — the ruleset is pre-1.0 (0.31.0, no tagged GitHub releases) and 0/6 exemplars exercise it, yet BZL-JAVA-24/27 are MUSTs resting entirely on reading its source. A round measuring its adoption outside this corpus, or its API churn across recent BCR versions, would tell us whether a MUST on a pre-1.0 dependency is defensible.

lcov→JaCoCo conversion ownership — BZL-JAVA-26 says any numeric floor is a CI script over the merged .dat, but names no tool. Whether a maintained lcov→Cobertura/JaCoCo converter exists that a dual Gradle+Bazel shop could standardise on was not run down; without one, a JVM shop needs two coverage toolchains with no bridge.
rule_ids: BZL-JAVA-01 — Pin all four JDK version flags in the root .bazelrc; never write the nonexistent --java_version/--tool_java_version. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-02 — Give both runtime flags a remotejdk_* value; treat local_jdk as a finding absent a comment. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-03 — Express a below-toolchain bytecode target as --javacopt "-source N -target N", never by lowering --java_language_version. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-04 — Never read an absent strict-deps flag as 'not enforced', and never write =off/=warn to make a build pass. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-05 — Write --experimental_strict_java_deps and confirm the spelling on the pinned binary before relying on it. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-06 — Wire Error Prone through --javacopt -Xep or java_package_configuration, never as a bazel_dep or maven coordinate. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-07 — Never disable header compilation without a recorded reason, and never call Bazel's header compiler 'ijar-based' — it is turbine. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-08 — Register the intended default JVM toolchain first and say so in a comment; never rely on 'more specific wins'. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-09 — Give a processor reading com.sun.tools.javac.* its own --add-exports jvmopt; never try to change JavaBuilder's --patch_module. (MUST where such a processor exists, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-10 — Set lock_file on every maven.install call and commit the file; one lock file per install tag. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-11 — Set fail_if_repin_required = True on every pinned maven.install; the default False makes both lock-file self-checks advisory. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-12 — Never hand-edit or line-merge maven_install.json; discard both sides and regenerate with REPIN=1 bazel run @maven//:pin. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-13 — Set strict_visibility = True on maven.install. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-14 — Set version_conflict_policy = "pinned" wherever the build claims deterministic resolution. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-15 — Scope every exclusion to the narrowest correct mechanism: per-artifact exclusions vs global excluded_artifacts. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-16 — Mark codegen-only coordinates neverlink and test-only ones testonly via maven.amend_artifact, never by hand-editing the generated target. (SHOULD, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-17 — Prefer the literal @maven//:group_artifact label over the artifact() macro in any BUILD file buildozer will touch. (CONSIDER, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-18 — Never let a Maven-resolved Kotlin jar reach a hand-rolled java_import; ijar strips inline-function bodies. (MUST, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-19 — Set kt_kotlinc_options(x_lambdas = "indy") wherever the same Kotlin sources are also compiled by Gradle. (MUST with a Gradle leg, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-20 — Know Kotlin compile actions run under persistent multiplexed workers by default; reach for --strategy=<mnemonic>=local first when triaging a Kotlin flake. (CONSIDER, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-21 — Name every _deploy.jar you ship explicitly; a green bazel build //... never builds it. (MUST for CLI/application consumers, unchanged)
BZL-JAVA-22 — In a dual Gradle+Bazel repo, require one prose line naming the canonical build; do not require a graph-parity verifier. (SHOULD, unchanged)

BZL-JAVA-23 — Decide contrib_rules_jvm's checkstyle/PMD/SpotBugs wrappers at the lint_setup()/linter.register() call, not at the bazel_dep; a transitive apple_rules_lint fetch is not adoption. (CONSIDER, REWRITTEN — scope narrowed, overclaim removed)

BZL-JAVA-24 — Run JUnit 5 under Bazel through contrib_rules_jvm's java_junit5_test or java_test_suite(runner = "junit5") with JUNIT5_DEPS added explicitly; a hand-rolled main_class must honour XML_OUTPUT_FILE, TESTBRIDGE_TEST_ONLY, TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE and TEST_SHARD_*. (MUST where a JUnit 5 suite runs under Bazel, NEW)
BZL-JAVA-25 — Never treat a transitively fetched apple_rules_lint as a linting adoption, and never add lint_setup()/linter.register() as part of a JUnit 5 change. (SHOULD, NEW)

BZL-JAVA-26 — Treat the single merged lcov _coverage_report.dat as Bazel's only Java coverage artifact and enforce any numeric floor as a CI step over it — never a Bazel flag, never per-target, never JaCoCo XML. (MUST where a coverage gate is claimed, NEW)
BZL-JAVA-27 — Pass runner = "junit5" explicitly on every java_test_suite over JUnit 5 sources; the default is junit4 and the failure is a green build that discovered zero tests. (MUST, NEW)

surprises: java-runtime-safety/find-sec-bugs-viability: find-sec-bugs 1.14.0 has a confirmed, reproduced NoSuchMethodError crash (not just a false-positive/staleness issue) against SpotBugs 4.9.5/4.9.6, caused by SpotBugs itself deleting a method it depended on — SpotBugs reverted the deletion within weeks, citing find-sec-bugs by name in its own PR.

java-runtime-safety/find-sec-bugs-viability: The deprecated method SpotBugs restored is scheduled for permanent removal ~1 year after 2025-10-08 (i.e. around October 2026, about a month after this research date), and find-sec-bugs's own unreleased master has already removed its usage — but no release has shipped that fix, so the public artifact will likely break again on schedule.

java-runtime-safety/find-sec-bugs-viability: Semgrep's public java ruleset explicitly cites find-sec-bugs.github.io/bugs.htm as the source-rule-url for ~24 of its 60 rules — Semgrep is not an independent alternative but a partial port of find-sec-bugs's own taxonomy, and it has zero rules for SchemaFactory/Validator/XMLReader/XPath XXE or PREDICTABLE_RANDOM.

java-runtime-safety/find-sec-bugs-viability: find-sec-bugs ships its SpotBugs dependency as provided scope, meaning the consumer's own toolVersion pin — not find-sec-bugs's declared version — determines actual runtime compatibility; the tool's own pom.xml version number is nearly irrelevant to whether it will crash.

java-runtime-safety/find-sec-bugs-viability: The exact same XXE cross-method false-negative (hardening applied in a helper method is invisible to the detector) was independently confirmed in both find-sec-bugs (#738) and SonarJava (S2755 community thread) — it's a structural limitation of single-method dataflow analysis shared across tools, not a find-sec-bugs-specific defect.

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: detekt's SwallowedException default config whitelists InterruptedException as 'nonexceptional' — the opposite gap direction from Java, where JAVA-ERR-01's mistake at least has an off-by-default Error Prone check to promote; no detekt rule ID exists for this at all

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: detekt's default gate is stronger than Java's for exception-chaining: SwallowedException (catches throw X(e.message)) is active by default, while Java's equivalent UnusedException is in Error Prone's DISABLED_CHECKS and must be promoted

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: runCatching's inlining means it never appears as a KtCatchClause at the call site, so every catch-clause-keyed detekt rule (SwallowedException, TooGenericExceptionCaught, EmptyCatchBlock) is structurally blind to it regardless of activation state

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: SuspendFunSwallowedCancellation (KT-CORO-01's sibling measurement) only fires when a suspend call happens inside runCatching's lambda — a non-suspend runCatching swallowing an Error/AssertionError has zero coverage under any detekt config

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: kotlin.Result's -Xallow-result-return-type restriction is fully historical (removed in Kotlin 1.5, 2021) yet still shows up in search results as if live — worth flagging explicitly so drafters don't cite it as current

java-runtime-safety/kotlin-errors-resources-and-throws: ktlint's 404'd public rules-doc page required falling back to reading the actual rule-class directory in the pinned exemplar clone, which is a stronger source anyway

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: The JDK-23 policy change was deferred mid-flight: proposed for JDK 22 (JDK-8306819), reverted to warning-only for that release (JDK-8321321), then reinstated a full release later for JDK 23 (JDK-8321319) -- three bug IDs for what reads as one release-note line

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: The origin motive is a supply-chain security concern (an unwitting dependency-shipped annotation processor auto-executing at compile time), not a build-hygiene cleanup

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: apache/maven's own POM shows both sides of the fix in one repo: pom.xml:135 sets proc=full reactor-wide, and submodule api/maven-api-di/pom.xml:34 explicitly overrides back to proc=none because that module only defines annotations and never processes them

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: Maven's toolchain story needs two rules, not one, because guava genuinely runs javac/javadoc on JDK 26 while Surefire tests the same build on JDK 8/11/17/25 via jdkToolchain -- a real, not hypothetical, split-JDK build

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: guava's own CI comment reveals the mechanism itself: -Dtoolchain.skip only works because actions/setup-java pre-installs every JDK the org.mvnsearch plugin would otherwise fetch -- a bare local mvn verify still needs that plugin (or a hand-built toolchains.xml)

maven-and-ant/maven-annotation-processing-and-toolchains: org.mvnsearch:toolchains-maven-plugin's Central metadata last-updated timestamp (April 2023) is years older than every other plugin queried here despite guava pinning its newest version, flagging an ecosystem-maturity risk for a mechanism the rule set would otherwise recommend as the standard fix

gradle-settings/settings-plugin-testkit-verification: No corpus exemplar (ktor's build-settings-logic, junit-framework's settings-conventions) and no gradle/gradle-own TestKit integration test ever applies a plugin from a functional test's generated settings.gradle — the mechanism is real but completely unexercised anywhere in the ecosystem read

gradle-settings/settings-plugin-testkit-verification: Gradle's own ConfigurationCacheTestKitIntegrationTest.groovy carries a doc comment explicitly naming both plugin-resolution routes (INJECTED_CLASSPATH via DefaultInjectedClasspathPluginResolver, MAVEN_REPO via DefaultScriptClassPathResolver) and parametrizes every test case over both — direct source confirmation of Q1/Q4 nobody had to infer

gradle-settings/settings-plugin-testkit-verification: There is no Gradle API, javadoc, or build-scan surface anywhere that reports how many times a shared BuildService was instantiated — registerIfAbsent's 'exactly once' is a construction-time guarantee, not an introspectable fact, so the assertion pattern (a marker file) had to be constructed rather than found
